title: docs(skills): teach the approval escalation clock (escalation.clock, escalation.calendar)
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-elon-musk"} -->
_Requested by **Elon** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9D?thread=cmsg_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9D4n2wzAmmp4Z6W5jsqtM2qx)_

Fixes #35931
Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 用户能看到什么变化:用 AI 写审批流程的作者,现在会被教到「审批超时可以按工作日历只算工作时间」,而不是旧的「平台没有工作日历」。
- 为什么做:属于「工作日历」这条线;超时按工作时间计算的功能已经上线,随包发布的技能文档还在教相反的说法。
- 出错会怎样:只改文档和一条评测用例,不改运行行为;写错了的后果是 AI 给出错误的配置建议,可直接撤回本次合并。
- 要你做什么:无(另有一处「平台目录仍写工作日历未提供」的遗留,见验收说明,需另行安排)。

## What changes

- `skills/objectstack-automation/references/state-machines-and-approvals.md`, the `escalation` row of the node-config table, rewritten in place from the merged contract (`ApprovalEscalationSchema` in `packages/spec/src/automation/approval.zod.ts`, `slaDeadline` in `packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.ts`, the lint in `packages/lint/src/validate-approval-approvers.ts`, the inbox label in `ui/apps/console/src/pages/system/ApprovalsInboxPage.tsx`). It now states:
  - both clocks and the default: `clock: 'wall_clock'` (default) counts nights, weekends and holidays; `'working_time'` counts `timeoutHours` as working hours on a working calendar (`sys_work_calendar`, maintained per organization in Setup);
  - the resolution order: the `calendar` code, else the organization's default, else refused, never wall-clock;
  - the cannot-answer hold: the request does not escalate, its row carries `sla_due_refusal` instead of `sla_due_at`, the inbox shows why, and each sweep retries;
  - the lint rule: `calendar` without `clock: 'working_time'` is the error `approval-escalation-calendar-without-working-time`.
- The sentence "the platform ships no business-hours calendar" is gone.
- Paid for inside the same file's ceiling by deletions (the ceiling row is untouched): the "Analog" column of the expression-roots table (other vendors' names for the three roots), the rationale sentence after "`record` and bare field names are NOT available" (the fix, `current.x` or `trigger.x`, stays), the pointer to a showcase flow in the framework repo (an installed app has no such repo), "the author declares keys, approvers only fill values" (the next sentences state the refusal of an undeclared key), "(do not mix them up)", and the `sys_user_position` parenthetical on `escalateTo`, which the Approver Types table's `position` row already carries.
- `skills/objectstack-data/references/data-hooks.md`: the note on a hook-stamped deadline says "wall-clock hours" instead of "calendar hours", names the constant `*_WALL_CLOCK_HOURS`, and points at `escalation.clock: 'working_time'` for an approval deadline. Same line count.
- `.changeset/35931-escalation-clock-skill.md`: `'@objectstack/skills': patch`.

## Evals

One case added, id 25 in `skills/objectstack-automation/evals/flows-triggers-approvals.json`: an approval step that must hand over after 8 business hours on the calendar `cn_plant`. It requires `clock: 'working_time'` and `calendar: 'cn_plant'` and refuses a hand-rolled `3_600_000` deadline. The old row would have answered that the platform has no working calendar, so the case separates the two texts.

`skills/objectstack-project/evals/project-process.json` case 8 is unchanged; see Acceptance notes.

## Verification

Head `d34c403632`. Read first: the `escalation` row (the one hunk that teaches new behaviour), then the five deletions in the same file. Two-minute check: `node scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs` prints `state-machines-and-approvals.md is 5932 tokens (ceiling 5936; headroom 4)` and `data-hooks.md is 10120 tokens (ceiling 10122; headroom 2)` and exits 0.

Readings, before to after:

| File | Lines | Bytes | Tokens / ceiling |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `state-machines-and-approvals.md` | 389 to 385 | 23710 to 23726 | 5928 to 5932 / 5936 |
| `data-hooks.md` | 884 to 884 | 40467 to 40478 | 10117 to 10120 / 10122 |
| `flows-triggers-approvals.json` (eval, not ratcheted) | 440 to 450 | 26920 to 28309 | 6730 to 7078 |

Whole catalog: authored 197404 to 197411 tokens (ceiling sum 202541 unchanged), shipped tree 288105 to 288460 tokens, of which 348 are the eval fixture; the sum of all `SKILL.md` files is 4944 lines before and after. Net added lines for the PR, changeset included: 33 added, 19 deleted, net 14 (budget 25).

Gates on this head, local: the `dispatch-gates --commands` list derived 49 commands; 45 exited 0, among them `check-skills-token-ratchet` and its self-test, `check:skill-refs`, `check:skill-served-sections`, `check:skill-identifier-liveness`, `check:skill-links`, `check:skill-compatibility`, `check:doc-authoring`, `check:nul-bytes`, `check-empty-changeset`, `check-adr-0087-registration` and `check:doc-formula-expressions` (after building its closure under the verify lock, `VERDICT command-exit 0`). NOT MEASURED: `check:dts-closure`, `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check:lean-entry-closure`, `check:sourcemap-no-sources-content`; each exited 3 asking for a full build, each reads built package output, and this diff changes no package, so they are left to CI. `overlap-check`: `VERDICT clean exit 0`.

## Acceptance notes

- **The project eval and the platform catalog are left as they are, and the catalog is now stale.** `skills/objectstack-project/references/platform-catalog.md` still lists working calendars under "Planned: carded, not shipped" as "not available", and project eval case 8 expects exactly that answer. The page is generated from `PLANNED_ROWS` in `packages/spec/scripts/lib/platform-catalog.ts`; `sys_work_calendar` and `sys_work_calendar_exception` are in the platform object registry and in Setup, and the approval clock reads them, but no catalog row names them. Changing the eval alone would make it contradict the page it is graded against, and moving the row is a generator edit with its own test and byte ceiling, which this card's diff does not carry. The three formula functions ADR-0157 D4 names are not in the formula stdlib on this head, so what the eval's "make the SLA formula read them" should now expect is not settled by what merged. Reported to the seat as a finding.
- **`data-hooks.md` renames the advised constant** from `*_CALENDAR_HOURS` to `*_WALL_CLOCK_HOURS`. The arithmetic the note teaches is unchanged and still true. The old name is the one the merged spec declined as a clock value because, with a working calendar in the platform, "calendar hours" reads as hours on that calendar. An app that followed the earlier advice has a constant whose name is now ambiguous; nothing refuses it.
- The row names `sla_due_refusal` and `sla_due_at` as fields of the request row; the three refusal codes are not listed, to stay inside the ceiling.
- No ablation or reverse verification: the diff changes prose, one eval fixture and a changeset, no tested behaviour.
